epistemic_role: Exact three-qubit operator-representation prerequisite, not a D4 ground-state, full star, action-conditioned instrument, or schedule experiment
question: Can the CZ factor displayed in Jing et al. Appendix A.1 Eq. (A2) be dropped while preserving even a local star-factor measurement law?

competing_models.source_factor: A = X_b CZ_{g,r}, one X factor and one disjoint CZ factor transcribed from a star-operator diagram; the complete star has further factors and is not simulated here.
competing_models.pauli_truncation: T = X_b, with the CZ factor omitted; this is an intentionally lossy diagnostic surrogate, not a proposed D4 model.

source: Jing et al., Intrinsic Heralding and Optimal Decoders for Non-Abelian Topological Order, Appendix A.1 Eq. (A2)-(A4), archived PDF printed page 10; https://arxiv.org/html/2507.23765
exact_matrix: For two qubit-label permutations, evaluate both A and T on |+,+,+> and |+,0,0>, with + on the X qubit. Use exact rational amplitudes/probabilities and all eight computational basis states. Check Hermiticity, involution, P_+ and P_- normalization, permutation covariance, and Pauli-character exclusion.
analysis_rule: A difference establishes only that the displayed CZ operator factor cannot be replaced by X alone for arbitrary local input states. It does not establish the distribution in the D4 ground space, a failure of the existing parity sampler, or a first-to-second conditional law.
acceptance: Pinned source and J6I hashes match; the A2 graphic contains both X and CZ factors in the same star operator.
Both local operators square to identity and yield normalized two-outcome projectors on both exact input classes under both label permutations.
The coherent input distinguishes source factor from truncated Pauli, while the Z-fixed control agrees; the source factor's CZ phase is not a Pauli-Z linear character.
No full-star D4, lattice action, public record, histories, schedule arms, bootstrap replicates, performance or threshold result is claimed.
stop_rule: Fail closed on source-image ambiguity, hash drift, operator algebra, exact probability, permutation or normalization mismatch. A pass only selects a CZ-aware representation requirement for the next full lattice fixture.
